headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors via shared MCP/stdin-stdout; data leakage and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a exposes stdin/stdout and MCP, and can execute shell/subprocesses; agent_b has broad network egress and API access. That creates a plausible bridge where content from agent_a can be treated as instructions by agent_b or vice versa. No provenance or isolation is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF agent_a output is forwarded into agent_b prompts or task payloads without provenance tags
IF either agent parses shared MCP/stdin content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable automatic forwarding between agents for one run
Wrap inter-agent messages in a fixed schema with explicit role labels
Add a one-line provenance prefix to every handoff
Review any MCP route that accepts free-form text
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, learning patterns, performance metrics, and task prompts, while agent_b touches workflow metadata and has broad egress. A shared workspace or handoff could leak sensitive repository context from agent_a into agent_b outputs or remote calls. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a workspace or message queue
IF agent_b sends received context to external services during normal operation
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories
Remove secrets and prompts from any shared handoff file
Turn off broad egress for the data-engineering agent during the test
Inspect logs for copied task prompts
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can modify git state, install packages, and execute shell commands; agent_b is an orchestrator with broad network egress and API calls. If both operate on the same repo or mutable workspace, they can race on git state or overwrite each other's changes. The profiles do not document locking, so the conflict is plausible in default pair usage.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same git repository or working tree
IF no external lock or lease is enforced around mutable resources
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree
Pause one agent while the other writes git state
Use a simple file lock around shared outputs
Check for uncommitted changes before each run
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency control to shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate outputs from shell/MCP workflows, and agent_b can orchestrate downstream actions. If agent_b treats agent_a's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect workflow actions or remote API calls. There is no documented verification step, but the profiles also do not show direct autonomous destructive actions, so medium fits.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without validation
IF agent_a output is used to trigger API calls or workflow steps
mitigations: Require a human review step for agent_a outputs
Add a checksum or schema validation on handoffs
Log the exact source of each downstream action
Limit agent_b to read-only dry runs first
requires-engineering: implement verification gates before action execution

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles repository metadata, task prompts, and Ed25519 signatures, while agent_b handles workflow metadata. No PHI, EU PII, or residency mismatch is documented, and both are open-source with docs-only evidence. The main compliance concern is retention/logging of prompts and metadata, which is narrower than a default breach scenario.
conditions: IF task prompts or repository metadata are retained in logs beyond the intended run
IF signatures or workflow metadata are exported to a third-party service
mitigations: Redact prompts from logs
Set short log retention for the test run
Confirm no PHI or regulated data enters the workflow
Export only aggregated metrics
requires-engineering: add policy checks for residency and retention
